Where it began

Jacob Duffy was born in Lumsden, in New Zealand's Southland region, and went to Southland Boys' High School in Invercargill. His first senior game came for Otago in January 2012, an HRV Cup match against Northern Districts, and Otago remained his home side for many seasons after.

The player

He became a hard-working mainstay of the Otago attack. In the 2017–18 Plunket Shield he shared top spot among Otago's wicket-takers with 29 in eight matches, and in the 2018–19 Ford Trophy he led their list outright with 25 in eleven games. His first game for New Zealand, a Twenty20 international against Pakistan on 18 December 2020, could hardly have gone better: 4 for 33 from his four overs and the player of the match award. He made his one-day international debut against Ireland in July 2022.

The Test cap took longer. He was named in New Zealand's squads for England in 2021, for the World Test Championship final that year and again for England in 2022, and each time the call to play did not come. It finally arrived in 2025, and he made up for lost time: his first 4 Tests brought him 25 wickets at an average of 16.28, with three five-wicket hauls and a best of 5 for 34.

What made him special

Persistence, mostly, and a knack for making an early impression. Counties in England noticed. Kent signed him for two Championship games in 2022, and on his debut he took eight wickets, including a five-wicket haul with three in a single over. Nottinghamshire brought him in for the end of their 2024 season, and Worcestershire for the first half of 2025.

His batting was more modest, though a top score of 36 and an average of 19.50 in Tests suggest he was nobody's idea of a walking wicket.

Away from the middle

Duffy's career is a good advertisement for staying the course. Between that first senior game for Otago and his first Test lay more than a decade of county stints, squad selections and seasons of hard work for Otago. When the chance came, he was ready for it.

And finally

Most bowlers would settle for 25 wickets in a whole season. Duffy managed them in his first 4 Tests, which suggests all that waiting in squads was time well spent studying the batsmen.
